decks.module: Alcohol amounts, BAC and legal conditions (A)

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The handbook warns that driving experience does not make drinking and driving safe, and that new drivers are more ____.
cards.back: The handbook warns that driving experience does not make drinking and driving safe, and that new drivers are more affected by alcohol while still learning.
cards.memory_hook: affected by alcohol while still learning

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The source treats twelve ounces of beer, five ounces of wine, and a cocktail containing one point five ounces of ____.
cards.back: The source treats twelve ounces of beer, five ounces of wine, and a cocktail containing one point five ounces of eighty-proof spirits as equal alcohol amounts.
cards.memory_hook: eighty-proof spirits as equal alcohol amounts

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Drinking and driving can bring heavy fines, higher insurance costs, loss ____.
cards.back: Drinking and driving can bring heavy fines, higher insurance costs, loss of the license and imprisonment.
cards.memory_hook: of the license and imprisonment

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Blood alcohol concentration describes alcohol in a quantity of blood as a ____.
cards.back: Blood alcohol concentration describes alcohol in a quantity of blood as a percentage determined by chemical analysis.
cards.memory_hook: percentage determined by chemical analysis

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The amount of alcohol consumed primarily controls how much alcohol reaches the bloodstream; food affects absorption to a lesser extent and drink ____.
cards.back: The amount of alcohol consumed primarily controls how much alcohol reaches the bloodstream; food affects absorption to a lesser extent and drink mixing has only a limited effect.
cards.memory_hook: mixing has only a limited effect

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The handbook’s example says two ounces of pure alcohol consumed within an hour produces about the same BAC regardless of ____.
cards.back: The handbook’s example says two ounces of pure alcohol consumed within an hour produces about the same BAC regardless of the type or mixture of drinks.
cards.memory_hook: the type or mixture of drinks

cards.back: The handbook’s weight example estimates that a one hundred-pound person needs about half the alcohol of a two hundred-pound person to reach the same BAC.
cards.memory_hook: person to reach the same BAC

cards.back: A driver can face a DUI charge even with a BAC below zero point zero eight.

cards.back: Refusing chemical testing may result in license revocation.

cards.back: The handbook warns that alcohol possession or consumption before age twenty-one can cause license revocation even without operating a vehicle.

cards.back: Alcohol slows reflexes and reactions, reduces clear vision and alertness, and worsens judgment as the amount in the body increases.

cards.back: Alcohol makes judging distance, speed and other vehicles’ movement more difficult and can interfere with vehicle control.

cards.back: The handbook’s advice is to avoid driving after drinking because even one drink can affect driving.

cards.back: Time is the only way to sober up; coffee, fresh air, exercise and cold showers do not provide a quick remedy.

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID table gives a minimum revocation of thirty to forty-five days ____.
cards.back: For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID table gives a minimum revocation of thirty to forty-five days before application eligibility, depending on BAC.
cards.memory_hook: before application eligibility, depending on BAC

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a second conviction, the IID table gives a sixty-day minimum revocation before ____.
cards.back: For a second conviction, the IID table gives a sixty-day minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications.
cards.memory_hook: application eligibility, subject to other qualifications

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a third conviction, the IID table gives a ninety-day minimum revocation before ____.
cards.back: For a third conviction, the IID table gives a ninety-day minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications.
cards.memory_hook: application eligibility, subject to other qualifications

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a fourth or later conviction, the IID table gives a six-month minimum revocation before ____.
cards.back: For a fourth or later conviction, the IID table gives a six-month minimum revocation before application eligibility, subject to other qualifications.
cards.memory_hook: application eligibility, subject to other qualifications

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: An IID license cannot be used for CDL-class vehicles or peripheral endorsements, and the qualifying offense must ____.
cards.back: An IID license cannot be used for CDL-class vehicles or peripheral endorsements, and the qualifying offense must not involve death or serious injury.
cards.memory_hook: not involve death or serious injury

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Other suspensions, revocations, disqualifications, denials or statutory disqualification criteria can prevent ____.
cards.back: Other suspensions, revocations, disqualifications, denials or statutory disqualification criteria can prevent issuance of an IID license.
cards.memory_hook: issuance of an IID license

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The general IID application process requires a valid Delaware license at the time of the offense, an application, the required treatment enrollment and fees, and surrender ____.
cards.back: The general IID application process requires a valid Delaware license at the time of the offense, an application, the required treatment enrollment and fees, and surrender of the currently issued Delaware license.
cards.memory_hook: of the currently issued Delaware license

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: An IID applicant must provide insurance proof for the vehicles on ____.
cards.back: An IID applicant must provide insurance proof for the vehicles on which devices will be installed.
cards.memory_hook: which devices will be installed

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The IID process requires proof of valid Delaware registration and installation on every vehicle the participant will operate during revocation, even a ____.
cards.back: The IID process requires proof of valid Delaware registration and installation on every vehicle the participant will operate during revocation, even a vehicle the participant does not own.
cards.memory_hook: vehicle the participant does not own

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Vision, knowledge and road-skills testing may be required before an ____.
cards.back: Vision, knowledge and road-skills testing may be required before an IID license is issued.
cards.memory_hook: IID license is issued

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: After all IID conditions are met, the DMV authorizes an approved vendor’s installation and verifies installation before issuing limited ____.
cards.back: After all IID conditions are met, the DMV authorizes an approved vendor’s installation and verifies installation before issuing limited driving privileges for the approved vehicles.
cards.memory_hook: driving privileges for the approved vehicles

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The IID participant pays all program costs and must keep devices installed for the required period, measured from IID license issuance rather ____.
cards.back: The IID participant pays all program costs and must keep devices installed for the required period, measured from IID license issuance rather than the original revocation end date.
cards.memory_hook: than the original revocation end date

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The IID duration table requires four months for ____.
cards.back: The IID duration table requires four months for a FOE participant.
cards.memory_hook: a FOE participant

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID duration table requires twelve to ____.
cards.back: For a non-FOE first conviction, the IID duration table requires twelve to twenty-three months, depending on BAC.
cards.memory_hook: twenty-three months, depending on BAC

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a second conviction, the IID duration table requires sixteen to ____.
cards.back: For a second conviction, the IID duration table requires sixteen to twenty-eight months, depending on BAC.
cards.memory_hook: twenty-eight months, depending on BAC

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: For a third conviction, the IID duration table requires twenty-one to ____.
cards.back: For a third conviction, the IID duration table requires twenty-one to thirty-three months, depending on BAC.
cards.memory_hook: thirty-three months, depending on BAC

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: The IID duration table requires at least fifty-four months for ____.
cards.back: The IID duration table requires at least fifty-four months for a fourth or later conviction.
cards.memory_hook: a fourth or later conviction

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: Noncompliance can cause the DMV to extend IID time ____.
cards.back: Noncompliance can cause the DMV to extend IID time or disqualify the participant.
cards.memory_hook: or disqualify the participant

cards.front: Complete the handbook statement: A DUI offender who does not apply for the IID program must serve the entire ____.
cards.back: A DUI offender who does not apply for the IID program must serve the entire revocation and cannot drive during it.
cards.memory_hook: revocation and cannot drive during it
